subject: leftover cooked rice
title: What If You Always Reheated Leftover Rice?

scenes.text: What if you always reheated rice that sat out overnight? The microwave can't save it.
Raw rice carries Bacillus cereus spores. They survive boiling, sometimes an hour at ninety degrees.
On the counter, they wake up and multiply fastest around thirty to forty degrees Celsius. Room temperature is plenty.
After a few hours, the bacteria make a toxin. It survives one hundred twenty-one degrees for over an hour.
So reheating kills bacteria, not the poison. Thirty minutes to six hours later, the vomiting starts.
The danger was never the reheating. It was the hours the rice sat out. Food agencies say cool it within one hour.

description:
What if you always reheated rice that was left out? Bacillus cereus spores survive cooking, multiply at room temperature, and make a vomiting toxin that survives about 121 degrees Celsius for over an hour, so reheating cannot remove it.
Symptoms start 0.5 to 6 hours after eating; Food Standards Scotland advises cooling rice within an hour, refrigerating it and reheating only once.
